answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-work identity minting: every new agent identity must solve a small hash puzzle before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fake personas costs a thousand times the compute. Think of it as a lantern each identity must light by hand; the violet flame only ignites once real work is spent, and that effort is what forges trust into the network. An attacker pays hardware and electricity per identity, which scales linearly and quickly outruns the rewards of a sybil swarm.
